units.source_text: 父亲的脸埋在初夏的花丛中。

en.t: My father's face was buried among the flowers of early summer.

units.source_text: 朵朵花儿都很娇嫩，水灵，甚至令人毛骨惊然，朵朵花儿好像在窥视着井底。

en.t: Every blossom was delicate and fresh, even chilling, as though each one were peering down into the bottom of the well.

units.source_text: 因为遗容是从活着的脸所具有的存在表面无限地陷落，只留下面对着我们的脸面的轮廓般的东西，一深陷下去就提不上来了。

en.t: Because the face left after death sinks endlessly away from the surface of existence that a living face possesses, leaving only something like the outline of a face turned toward us; once it has sunk deep, it can no longer be raised back up.

units.source_text: 再没有什么比遗容更能如实地告诉我：所谓物质，距我们是多么遥远，它的存在方法是多么不可企及啊！

en.t: Nothing told me more plainly than a dead person's face how far away so-called matter is from us, and how unreachable its way of existing is.

units.source_text: 精神就这样通过死变成物质，我第一次能够接触到这样一种局面。

en.t: In this way, through death, spirit becomes matter, and for the first time I was able to come into contact with such a condition.

units.source_text: 现在我才渐渐理解5月的花卉、太阳、桌子、校舍、铅笔……等等物质为什么对我那样冷漠，距我那样遥远。

en.t: Only now did I gradually begin to understand why the flowers of May, the sun, the table, the school building, the pencil, and other such material things were so cold toward me and so far away from me.
That was where the reason lay.
